summary.name: LosslessCut
summary.one_liner: LosslessCut is a video and audio cutting tool that trims, joins and converts media by copying the data stream directly, without re-encoding, so cuts are fast and lossless.
keywords: lossless cutter alternative to traditional video editors
use_cases: Cut commercials out of a recorded TV show
Extract the music track from a video
Add music to a video or replace its audio
Join clips from the same camera or phone
Cut a file by its MP4 or MKV chapters
Trim video quickly without quality loss
summary.what_it_does: LosslessCut cuts the data stream of a media file and copies it directly, avoiding the full re-encode that traditional video editors require, which the page says makes operations take seconds instead of hours. Example uses on the page include removing commercials from TV recordings, converting TS to MP4, extracting audio tracks, replacing or adding audio, joining clips, and cutting by MP4/MKV chapters. The page notes that available functions depend on the file's format and codecs, and that lossless cuts can only start at a keyframe, so a cut may begin a fraction of a second up to several seconds before the requested point. It is described as open source, with code viewable on GitHub.
notable: Stream copy editing: cuts without re-encoding, so no quality loss and very fast
Open source with no ads or tracking, per the FAQ
Free on GitHub; paid versions in Microsoft Store and Apple App Store offer signed builds and auto-updates
caveats: Cuts can only start at keyframes, so cut points may be a few seconds early depending on encoding
Available functions depend on the file's format and codecs
Paid purchase on app stores is optional; the Microsoft Store charges for the signed version, while GitHub downloads are free and unsigned
